# Workday

Workday sits at the center of many enterprise TA stacks and owns Paradox, an AI-driven recruiting platform. Workday faces two critical pressure points: first, litigation over AI bias in its screening tools (Mobley v. Workday), where a judge let claims proceed that treat the vendor as liable for algorithmic discrimination alongside employers; second, ownership risk following Silver Lake's reported talks to take the company private, which could trigger roadmap and compliance shifts affecting both the core HCM suite and Paradox's product direction. For TA teams running Workday's recruiting modules or Paradox directly, procurement risk spans both legal exposure and potential leadership changes under new ownership.

## Timeline

- **22 Jun 2026** — A federal judge let the Mobley v. Workday AI-bias suit proceed, with Judge Rita Lin's 22 June order allowing FEHA and ADA claims to move toward trial and treating the vendor as an "agent" of employers — meaning your ATS vendor's flaws can become your liability. TA leaders should inventory every AI screening tool, demand bias-audit documentation, and lock in human-review checkpoints now. — [SHRM](https://www.shrm.org/topics-tools/news/technology/workday-ai-lawsuit-wake-up-call-hr)

- **22 Jun 2026** — A California federal judge (Rita Lin) ruled Workday must face state FEHA discrimination claims, finding a sufficient California nexus because its AI screening tools are built and maintained there — extending exposure to employers nationwide and reinforcing that "the vendor's algorithm did it" is not a defense. TA leaders should re-examine vendor contracts, bias audits, and human-oversight documentation now. — [HR Dive](https://www.hrdive.com/news/workday-california-AI-bias-lawsuit-feha/823555/)

- **13 Aug 2026** — Private equity firm Silver Lake is in talks to take Workday private in what would rank among the largest software buyouts ever, sending the stock up sharply before a volatility halt. Workday owns Paradox and sits at the center of many enterprise TA stacks, so any leadership or roadmap shift under new ownership is a procurement risk to raise in your next vendor review. — [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/13/workday-skyrockets-25percent-before-trading-halted-on-report-of-silver-lake-takeover.html)

- **19 Oct 2026** — Workday and Anthropic are connecting Claude with Sana agents while keeping HR permissions, approvals and audit controls anchored in Workday — relevant for TA teams that want governed AI inside an existing HCM rather than a bolt-on. — [Workday Extends Governed HR and Finance Workflows Into Claude](https://futurumgroup.com/insights/workday-extends-governed-hr-and-finance-workflows-into-claude/)

## Open questions

- How will Workday's compliance posture and Paradox investment roadmap change under private equity ownership?
- Will settlements in the Mobley suit reshape how Workday and other vendors approach bias auditing and human oversight?
